paper.title_en: Study of Radiative Muon Capture Experimental Data and its Implications for Muon-Conversion Experiments
paper.abstract_en: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. We develop a model characterized by distinct nucleon-knockout final states, each with its associated multibody phase space and kinematic endpoint. This framework is applied to photon data from TRIUMF and positron data from SINDRUM II, and the results are compared to the previously used closure approximation. We find that separately modeling the distinct nucleon-knockout final states provides an improved description of the available RMC data near the endpoint, and we discuss the implications for the COMET and Mu2e experiments.
